_source: Live capture from a real PMS (SFLIX), 2026-07-28, via PlexTvClient.list_users().
_why: plex-safety rule 11: any assumption about a plex.tv response shape gets a recorded fixture.
The assumption this pins is the one behind privacy.py's decision to SKIP share-filter writes for
restricted accounts. Note what is actually here: the account carries filterMovies/filterTelevision
already, but they are a contentRating= parental-control filter, NOT label!=. So:
1. A restricted account CAN hold share filters — 'restricted' does not mean 'no filters'.
2. Merging label excludes in is mechanically ordinary: contentRating= is just another condition
for merge_label_excludes to byte-preserve alongside a new label!= one.
3. This account HAS a rating profile set. The 2026-07-25 note that a restricted account 'sees
ZERO collections' was therefore recorded against a profiled account — which is exactly the
distinction issue #20's reporters draw (managed users with NO age restriction see everything).
Values are URL-encoded exactly as plex.tv returned them and must stay that way: parse/serialize
round-trips raw strings, never decoded ones.
